abstract: This postdoctoral research project develops and validates an uncertainty-aware, end-to-end decision framework for crop water-stress monitoring and irrigation decision support, applied to tomato (RQ1) on Hungarian farms accessed through the associated partner AgroVIR. It fuses multi-source Earth observation (Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, and secured high-resolution PlanetScope imagery), meteorological data (ERA5 reanalysis) and field observations into probabilistic estimates of the latent field state - root-zone soil moisture and crop water status (RQ3) - carrying uncertainty honestly from observation to decision. The project adopts Route B, the homogeneous-patch proxy (RQ2): it sidesteps the sub-pixel resolution problem by reading a nearby covarying patch that the coarse pixel can resolve cleanly, within a methodological architecture that also defines a rigorous one-step probabilistic-fusion alternative (Route A). From the diagnosed state onward, the state drives uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration and counterfactual irrigation simulation over weather ensembles, recommending the option that best improves water-use efficiency (WUE, RQ6). Diagnosis and decisions are validated against non-destructive physiological ground truth - chlorophyll fluorescence, stomatal conductance, canopy/leaf temperature and spectral reflectance (RQ4) - with uncertainty calibration judged by prediction-interval coverage (90% intervals containing the truth about 90% of the time, RQ5) and Route B's patch covariation established by a co-located seasonal campaign measuring the target crop and the proxy patch simultaneously (RQ9). The scientific novelty, argued against a systematic literature review, is the end-to-end coupling of learned multimodal fusion, explicit probabilistic crop-water-state estimation and water-use-efficiency-oriented irrigation, delivered as a research prototype (TRL 3-4, RQ10), which the literature reports as underdeveloped.
